events.title: SAP
about: General Admission (Standing) - Doors open at 7PM $15 Advanced, $20 Day of Show SAP is an independent, alternative rock trio from Austin, TX. Infusing the energetic and melodic sonics of 90’s grunge with emotionally driven dynamics of contemporary music, Sap creates a perfect soundscape for unpredictable live shows. The band is composed of guitarist/vocalist Evan Fundora, bassist Hank Barna, and drummer Jared Cox. Together they have accrued over 6 million streams worldwide, touring with longstanding bands like The Jins and most recently with up and coming acts such as Clarion, Rehash and Cheerleader Roadkill. Sap is set to go on their own US tour in support of their new 2026 album ‘Erasure’.
Channelling the high-energy, heavy breakdowns of 2000s post-hardcore, paired with melodic vocals that soar, SIR ECHO are a force to be reckoned with hailing from Upstate New York’s alternative scene.
Known for their razor-sharp riffs, cathartic choruses, and haunting melodies, their songs are a crashing ocean wave of emotion, and simultaneously, are the lighthouse guiding the ship home.

Gathered from the dynamic tango of harsh and clean vocals of Alexisonfire, stylistically blended with introspective intensity adjacent to Hail The Sun, the amalgamation of influences give the band a distinctive texture in the emo/alternative space.
Their latest release ‘To Fly With Clipped Wings’ (Produced by Alan Day of Four Year Strong), is the band’s debut EP released with Equal Vision Records.

Sludge Mother is a sonic force reigniting the raw energy of 1990's rock anthems. Channeling the heavy, sludgy riffs of Soundgarden and the emotive depth of Alice In Chains, Sludge Mother is resurrecting grunge’s soul, reimagined for a new era. Sludge Mother, known for her intense vocals and unfiltered lyricism, fuses the grit of Seattle’s golden age with a modern, visceral intensity. The result is a sound that’s both familiar and fresh—drenched in fuzzed-out guitars, brooding melodies, and the kind of anthemic choruses that demand to be shouted in dimly lit venues.

events.title: POKEY LAFARGE & His Band
about: $30 advanced, $35 day of show General Admission (Standing) - Doors open at 7PM For two decades, Pokey LaFarge has walked his own effortlessly cool road as an exceptionally iconoclastic troubadour – forthright, genuine, and markedly keen to put it all out there. Rent Money now sees him pushing forward yet again in what can be safely declared his finest collection to date, both as an heartfelt expression of personal experience and as no-nonsense social commentary. With its twanging guitars, plucky rhythms, and undeniably captivating melodies, the album soars and swings, its joyous refrains belying the inescapable undercurrent of constant worry and angst that permeates these troubled times. As always, the Illinois native deftly traverses the genre boundaries, seamlessly integrating the myriad strains of 20th-century American music with a freewheeling command of earnest songcraft, inspired performance, and subversive creativity. Rent Money stands tall as an indisputable high-water mark for Pokey LaFarge – a defining collection from a one-of-a-kind artist of rare ingenuity and uncommon candor, now as ever, determinedly crafting a sure-footed brand of deeply human music all his own.

“People are always going to tell you what they think you should play,” says Pokey LaFarge, “what you should sing about, how you should sound, how you should look, how you should act. And I’ve always just been like, nah. Nope. I’ve just completely gone my own way, and hopefully I’ve been honest and authentic in the process.

“I’m just trying to make music that AI can’t replicate. Things are so homogenized right now. That’s what I’m really, really, really resistant to, especially when it comes to music. I’m not going to do it. I’m not going to conform.”

Born and raised in Georgia, this talented pair imitates and modernizes folk music to a rejuvenating degree. The sound of Andrea DeMarcus and Dave Kirslis exhibits skilled and articulate guitar picking honed in the dive bars of Atlanta over rolling Julliard-trained bass lines. Expect chilling harmonies, unbridled enthusiasm, some wholesome tunes and a sincere performance.

events.title: Kaleta & Super Yamba Band
about: $20 advanced, $25 day of show General Admission (Standing) - Doors at 7PM Brooklyn’s Kaleta & Super Yamba Band are fronted by Afrobeat and Juju veteran Leon Ligan-Majek a.k.a. Kaleta. The singer/guitarist from the West African country of Benin Republic lived his adolescent life in Lagos, Nigeria where Afrobeat was born. Kaleta's guitar chops earned him decades of touring and recording with Fela Kuti, King Sunny Ade, Lauryn Hill and more. Kaleta got his start in the late 70s performing in church and was soon after picked up by iconic Juju master and world music pioneer King Sunny Ade. A few years later Fela Kuti came calling. Kaleta would go on to tour the world playing guitar for the King of Afrobeat in his storied band Egypt 80 through the 1980s and into the 1990s. Now based in New York City, Kaleta has been leading Super Yamba Band since 2017.

Their debut album 'Mèdaho,' which was released by California indie label Ubiquity Records, draws on the group’s shared reverence for the raw, psychedelic sounds that captivated Kaleta as a music loving kid in 1970s Benin. Mèdaho means "big brother", "elder" or "teacher" and is dedicated to Kaleta's late brother Ligan-Ozavino Pascal who introduced him to funk and soul music at a very early age. The album was included on Bandcamp's “Best Albums of Summer 2019” list and two of the songs were chosen for the ABC/Hulu series High Fidelity staring Zoe Kravitz. Kaleta and his band have also erupted onto the stages and video screens of major music festivals and music publications across the US.

events.title: The BONES of J.R. Jones
about: <a href=" class="sqs-block-button-element--medium sqs-button-element--primary sqs-block-button-element" data-sqsp-button
> TICKETS
$22 advanced, $25 day of show General Admission (Standing) - Doors open at 7PM Growing up, Jonathon Linaberry was obsessed with the radio.

“I remember sitting there at night, glued to the boombox, cassette player ready to record whenever my favorite songs came on,” he recalls. “There was something so thrilling about it, something romantic that I think we’ve lost now that everything’s available at our fingertips. I wanted to find a way to get back to that place, to recapture those feelings of excitement and anticipation and possibility.”

Linaberry does precisely that on Radio Waves, his sixth studio album as The Bones Of J.R. Jones. Recorded in Toronto with producer Robbie Lackritz (Feist, Bahamas), the collection is moody and hypnotic, steeped in the sonic landscape of the ’80s and ’90s as it excavates the past with equal parts nostalgia and curiosity. The arrangements are utterly entrancing here, built on the tension between acoustic instruments and retro synthesizers, and Linaberry’s performances are raw and visceral, at times aching in their vulnerability. Put it all together and you’ve got a poignant exploration of memory and longing delivered by a relentless searcher, a revelatory work of personal reflection steeped in the endless beauty, pain, and chaos of youth.

“I’ve never really resonated with the idea of ‘the good old days,’” Linaberry reflects. “Your understanding of the past and your relationship with it change as you get older, and I’ve always been more interested in the evolution of those feelings than in wearing any kind of rose-colored glasses.”

Born and raised in central New York, Linaberry got his start playing in hardcore and punk bands before becoming enamored with the field recordings of Alan Lomax, who documented rural American blues, folk, and gospel musicians throughout the 1930s and ’40s. Inspired by the unvarnished honesty of those vintage performances, Linaberry launched The Bones of J.R. Jones in 2012 and, operating as a fully independent artist, began releasing a series of critically acclaimed albums and EPs that would land his songs in a slew of films and television shows (including True Detective, Suits, Daredevil, Longmire, and Graceland) and lead to countless tours across the US and Europe (including…

$25 advanced, $30 day of show General Admission (Standing) - Doors open at 7PM BAILEN is a songwriting-forward, indie pop, folk-rock band that has captivated audiences with their musical dynamism and the three-part “blood harmony” of siblings Julia (guitar), Daniel (bass), and David (drums). The trio was raised by two freelance classical musicians in New York City who steeped them in Rock & Roll and Brahms. Their close familial bond is evident in their tight-knit musical arrangements and rich, emotive harmonies.

The group has released two studio albums, Thrilled to Be Here (2019), produced by John Congelton, and Tired Hearts (2023), produced by Brad Cook. Both albums showcase their knack for crafting infectious melodies and introspective lyrics, earning them critical acclaim and a dedicated fan base.

Their debut album was hailed by Rolling Stone as an “impressive debut”, in which they were compared to CSN, Fleetwood Mac, TLC, and Haim. Their catalog has over 50 million streams, and their song “I Was Wrong” reached the top 20 on Billboard’s Adult Alternative Chart. Additionally, NPR voted their song “Something Tells Me” #5 on the Best Songs of 2019. The band has made several TV appearances as featured artists, performing on the CBS Morning Show and The Today Show. They’ve also had the privilege of working with so many artists they admire, releasing collaborations with Amos Lee and Trousdale in 2024.

In addition to their studio work, BAILEN is renowned for their engaging live performances, which feature a blend of heartfelt ballads and high-energy anthems. With a history of touring with the likes of Hozier, Amos Lee, The Lone Bellow, and many more, their stage presence and chemistry have made them a standout act at various music festivals and venues across the country.

Currently, BAILEN is preparing to release their third full-length album, which they engineered and produced themselves with collaborators Jake Sinclair (Panic! At The Disco), Riccardo Damian (Sampha), and Chris Tabron (The Strokes). They are excited to release this record fully independent.

about: <a href=" class="sqs-block-button-element--medium sqs-button-element--primary sqs-block-button-element" data-sqsp-button
> TICKETS

$15 advanced, $20 day of show General Admission (Seated) - Doors open at 7PM Across his rollicking new LP Big Jefe, Jack Blocker fully embraces the rough-edged Americana spirit that’s called to him from the start. The 28-year-old singer-songwriter muses on nights out drinking, making mistakes, and life on the road across the project’s eleven tracks. Blocker didn’t set out to make a concept album. During his first winter in Nashville, he started writing a new tune over a few pours of whiskey – one that made him chuckle and feel excited about songwriting again. The song became “Big Jefe,” Blocker’s first ever single that tells the tale of a reckless, drunken miscreant named Jefe, released in 2023. He started dreaming up a world around that story, inspired in part by Willie Nelson’s 1975 concept album Red Headed Stranger, as well as country singer-songwriters like Marty Robbins and Townes Van Zandt.

A native of Richardson, Texas, Blocker grew up playing music in church. When a friend with an impressive vinyl collection played him records by songwriting greats like Johnny Cash, he started writing music of his own. After playing shows in college, he moved to Nashville in 2022 to pursue music full-time and never looked back. In addition to his own headline shows, Blocker opened for artists like Shane Smith and the Saints, Molly Tuttle, Hayes Carll and Drake Milligan, with live shows serving as deep inspiration for Big Jefe.

Produced by Patrick Lyons (Colter Wall, Noeline Hofmann), Big Jefe is about transformation. It’s a story about a drifter – a broke drunkard searching for purpose. Drawn into the drug trade out of perceived necessity, he chases opportunity and transforms a struggle for survival into an unlikely rise to power as Big Jefe. Big Jefe is set for a November 6 release via Thirty Tigers / Elbow Grease Records. It’s Blocker’s first project with Thirty Tigers, marking an exciting new chapter in his career.

Already a veteran of the road at 28, Blocker’s sound sits at the intersection of outlaw country, Americana folk, and the Texas singer-songwriter tradition. Last year, he released his debut album, The Land On Most High, produced by Big Jefe producer Patrick Lyons and released on his own label, Elbow Grease Records and his…

events.title: BOSS BARITONES - Gary Smulyan & Frank Basile
about: $10 cover, $5 for students (free to jam)

General Admission (Seated) - Doors open at 7PM Inspired by the rich history of the great 2-tenor pairings in jazz (think Lester Young & Herschel Evans, Gene Ammons & Sonny Stitt, Lockjaw Davis & Johnny Griffin, and Al Cohn & Zoot Sims), the Boss Baritones continue this tradition, but with the pairing of the tenor saxophone's lower pitched baritone brethren.
So who are these "Boss Baritones?" Locking horns in the front line are two of today's finest exponents and practitioners of the baritone saxophone in jazz: Gary Smulyan and Frank Basile.

Gary Smulyan has been steadily polishing his craft for over 40 years and is all but unanimously regarded as today's leading baritone saxophonist. Since filling the baritone chair in Woody Herman's Young Thundering Herd in 1978, Smulyan has gone on to perform with virtually every important name in jazz since. A sampling of this lofty company includes the Mel Lewis Jazz Orchestra, the Gene Harris Superband, B.B. King, Joe Henderson, Freddie Hubbard, Michel Camilo, the Carnegie Hall Jazz Band, Cedar Walton, Joe Lovano, George Coleman, the Mingus Big Band, and Dave Holland. A favorite of critics and peers alike, Smulyan has consistently topped polls in Downbeat, Jazz Times, and with the Jazz Journalists Association for the past two decades. Smulyan is a 6-time Grammy winner.

Frank Basile made his way on to the New York scene in 2001 after his studies at the University of North Texas and a brief stint at the Juilliard School. He has since forged his own path following in the footsteps of his mentors such as Smulyan. Dubbed a "prized sideman" by The New Yorker, Basile has been called upon to perform with the Vanguard Jazz Orchestra, the Dizzy Gillespie All-Star Big Band, the Jimmy Heath Big Band, the Bob Mintzer Big Band, the Jon Faddis Jazz Orchestra, the Christian McBride Big Band, the Count Basie Orchestra, and the Duke Ellington Orchestra. As a "rising star," Basile has consistently appeared in the Downbeat critic's poll since 2014.

The Boss Baritones made their debut the weekend of March 6-7, 2020 at Smalls Jazz Club in New York City. General Admission - Standing plus seating available *Ticketing via UMass FAC Box Office Italian singer-songwriter Maria Mazzotta spent much of her career celebrating and exploring the nuances of the traditional music of her home region, Apulia’s Salento peninsula, first as a member of the internationally renowned ensemble Canzoniere Grecanico Salentino, then in her early solo work.

Mazzotta’s 2020 album, Amoreamaro, is both a gorgeous collection of open, emotional performances and a fascinating document of a musician and composer exploring the edges of a tradition awash in international influence. Mazzotta’s music on that effort ventures out from Salento (the heel of Italy’s boot) finding influences from across the Adriatic, Ionian, and Mediterranean, and shaping a sound at once fundamentally Pugliese and intriguingly international.

On her most recent release, 2024’s Onde, Mazzotta tears up whatever was left of her initial script to deliver a profoundly brilliant work in which Salentino tradition forms the foundation of a sound that not only pulls influence from southern Europe and northern Africa but layers in fuzzy, gritty post-rock experimentation. Mazzotta, along with percussionist Cristiano Della Monica and guitarist Ernesto Nobili, set out to create a collection of songs that move and vary like the sea (onde translates to waves). And they accomplished exactly that, capturing the calm, the fury, the raw power, and the infinite changeability of tides in a collection of traditional and original songs that is impossible to set aside. Entrancing, captivating, enveloping, Onde pulls the listener in and works its will in a manner that reflects Mazzotta’s live performances. With her commanding voice and dynamic stage presence, Mazzotta makes every concert an immersive experience. Join us to see, hear, and feel it for yourself.

events.title: King Tuff x Sheer Mag
about: $25 advanced, $28 day of show General Admission (Standing) - Doors open at 7PM There are times in our life when we feel magic in the air. When new love arrives, or we find ourselves lost in a moment of creation with others who share our vision. A sense that: this is who I want to be. This is what I want to share.
It’s a fleeting feeling and one that Kyle Thomas, the singer-songwriter who records and performs as King Tuff, found himself longing for in the spring of 2020.

But knowing he couldn’t simply recreate this time in his life at will, Thomas—who hails from Brattleboro, Vermont—set out to write a love letter to those cherished moments of inspiration and to the small town that formed him. The one where he first nurtured his songwriting impulses, bouncing ideas off other like-minded artists. The kind of place where the changing of the seasons always delivered a sense of perspective and fresh artistic inspiration. Where he felt a deeper connection with nature and sense of community that had once been so close at hand.
“I wanted to make an album to remind myself that life is magical,” he reflects.
And so, Thomas seized upon his memories, creating what he calls “an album about love and nature and youth.”

The result is Smalltown Stardust, a spiritual, tender and ultimately joyous record that might come as a shock to those with only a passing knowledge of the artist’s back catalog. On Smalltown Stardust, Thomas takes us on his journey to a place where past and present collide, where he can be a dreamer in love with all that he sees. Images of his youth abound: from Route 91 which runs through his hometown (in “Smalltown Stardust”); to Redtooth, a spectre who used to roam the streets (“Bandits Of Blue Sky”); to old friends, old haunts and old dreams (“Always Find Me”); to Vermont’s Rock River, which gave its name to a song of a torch still burning for past love: “Those days are gone and we can’t rewind/ Cuz people grow and places change/ But my love for you will never fade away.”

Underlying every great record, every career-defining work of art, is a certain ineffable, increasingly rarified quality: unity of vision. Great songs need not announce their greatness: their marriage of idea with action, soul with sound, appears as something which is naturally effortless, unforced—they are what they are because they have no choice but to be. Amber performs solo, with Zizia, and the duo, Ganesh and Wolfe. Her forthcoming album, Half of Dust, will be released in November 2026 by Sedimental and Feeding Tube records.

Amber has been part of the ecological sound art group Zizia since 2018. She and Jarrod Fowler collaborated with Michael Pisaro-Liu as the group Pisaura, which released Asteraceae (Sedimental, 2020). Zizia’s album, Genera (hibari, 2023) includes sonic contributions from 36 other musicians. Recently, Amber has begun performing with improviser Ananya Ganesh as Ganesh & Wolfe.

As Amber Wolfe, she composes and performs folk songs with guitar and voice. Her familiarity with mythology, folklore, and fairytales weave throughout her lyrics, which reflect her connection to the cycles of the natural world. Amber accompanies herself with minimalist guitar, often in nonstandard tunings derived from ancient associations between the planets and musical scales.

Wolfe’s compositions often reflect the practice of astrological indeterminacy, whereby she selects tones that reflect the position of the planets at the time of a concert or recording. Her masters thesis, Tone Art: Astrology, Anthroposophy, Music details her approach to astrological indeterminacy and its connection to the philosophy of Rudolf Steiner, founder of Waldorf Education.
Amber was born and raised in Takoma Park, Maryland, lived for many years in Massachusetts’ Connecticut River Valley, and now resides on the New Hampshire seacoast.

Beth Kaplan founded the Boston band Salem 66 with guitarist Judy Grunwald and drummer Susan Merriam in 1981. Known for haunting vocals and melodic bass lines, Salem 66 released five records on New York's Homestead label before breaking up in 1990.

In 2025, Don Giovanni Records remastered the long out-of-print original recordings and released them for the first time on the streaming services along with SALT, a new vinyl /CD compilation, featuring liner notes by Franklin Bruno, essays from the two songwriters, and a slew of previously unpublished photos. As Rolling Stone put it, "lost 1980s Indie rock pioneers Salem 66 are getting their moment in the sun."
The 2025 re-release prompted Chris Brokaw (Come, Codeine) to invite Beth to play at his…

events.title: KARRIN ALLYSON - Northampton Jazz Workshop
about: $10 cover at the door, $5 students, free to jam General Admission (Seated) - Doors open at 7PM Jam session after the show - bring your axe to sit in!

Karrin Allyson, 5-­‐time Grammy nominated jazz vocalist, pianist, and songwriter is widely recognized as one of the most gifted voices of her generation. She has built a mastery of The Great American Songbook, blues, pop, be-­‐bop, Brazilian, and French chansons, to name a few.

Allyson rose to prominence in the ‘90s, releasing a string of albums including her debut I Didn’t Know About You in 1992 and picking up Best Jazz Vocal Album Grammy nominations for 2001's Ballads: Remembering John Coltrane, 2006’s Footprints, 2007’s Imagina: Songs of Brasil, 2011's 'Round Midnight, and 2015’s Many a New Day: Karrin Allyson Sings Rodgers and Hammerstein.

Born in Great Bend, Kansas, Allyson now lives in New York City, after growing up in Omaha, Nebraska and earning her bachelor’s degree in Piano Performance from the University of Nebraska at Omaha. She spent time in both Kansas City and Minneapolis before making the move in 2000. Also an accomplished vocal instructor, Allyson travels the world teaching, touring, and playing the major jazz festivals, concert venues, and clubs of the U.S. and overseas.

Allyson’s impressive discography culminated last year with the release of Some of that Sunshine, her first collection of all-­‐original songs. The record unleashes her dexterity as a songwriter and includes tracks that touch on social change and romantic disillusion while maintaining a joyous, bittersweet optimism.

With fifteen albums released so far, and always more exciting projects in the works, Allyson’s range and creativity seems to have no bounds. What unites this wide world of music is Allyson’s warmth and depth. She’s not just singing a lyric, she’s telling you her story. And then that becomes your story. You hear the music from the inside out.
Karrin is a storyteller who swings and is singing to YOU - with songs in the key of NOW!

events.title: La Pena Máxima 2
about: Únase a la productora de cine María Isabel Pâramo y al actor Biassini Segura para una sesión de preguntas y respuestas en vivo después de la proyección de su película, La Pena Máxima 2.

Colombia está a un partido de clasificar al Mundial, pero un cambio inesperado hace que el encuentro coincida con la boda de Laura, la hija de Abelardo, con el jugador estrella de la Selección. Para complicarlo todo, Abelardo ha apostado el dinero de la luna de miel a que su futuro yerno marcará tres goles.

Entre la pasión por el fútbol, el amor por la familia y una cadena de divertidos enredos, La pena máxima 2 es una comedia colombiana capaz de conectar con públicos de todas las culturas. Porque hay emociones y celebraciones que no necesitan traducción.
Proyectada en español con subtítulos en inglés.
FREE with reservations
Join movie producer María Isabel Pâramo and actor Biassini Segura for a live Q&A following the screening of their film, La Peña Máxima 2.

Colombia is just one match away from qualifying for the World Cup, but an unexpected schedule change means that the game will take place on the same day as the wedding of Abelardo’s daughter, Laura, to the national team’s star player. To make matters worse, Abelardo has bet the honeymoon money on his future son-in-law scoring a hat trick.

Blending a passion for soccer, the love of family, and a hilarious chain of mishaps, La Pena Máxima 2 is a Colombian comedy that can connect with audiences across cultures because some emotions, and celebrations, need no translation.
Screened in Spanish with English subtitles.

events.title: Close Encounters With Music: Saluting the Clarinet – Mozart, Beethoven, Bartok and Gershwin
about: $35 Balcony / $60 Orchestra (plus processing fees)
Wednesday, August 26 at noon · Friday, August 28 at noon

Members receive $5 off each ticket It can come on brash and it can come on sensuous. In the orchestra, it steps forward in "Peter and the Wolf" and "Rhapsody in Blue"; in opera it's a near-protagonist in "The Magic Flute," "La Traviata" and "The Barber of Seville" as composers delineate atmosphere and character motifs. It can sing and it can swing. We are referring of course to the clarinet, which stars in a program that features Bartók's "Contrasts," written for clarinet legend Benny Goodman and violinist Joseph Szigeti (with Bartók himself playing the piano at the world premiere!); Beethoven's Trio in B-flat major, opus 11; Mozart's Clarinet Quintet, and some down-home Gershwin. The program abounds in Hungarian country fiddling and dance melodies, rich folk fare and jazz, as well as clarinet and violin pyrotechnics. The remarkable clarinetist Alexander Fiterstein will leave us all breathless! He is joined by pianist Michael Chertock, violinist Xiao-Dong Wang and cellist and artistic director Yehuda Hanani.
Alexander Fiterstein, clarinet; Michael Chertock, piano; Xiao-Dong Wang, Helena Baillie, violins; Daniel Panner, viola; Yehuda Hanani, cello

See Lesley Manville and Aidan Turner star in the National Theatre’s striking production of Les Liaisons Dangereuses, a classic tale of seduction, ambition and social intrigue.
The pen is mightier than the sword.
Among the glittering salons of the super-rich, patriarchy equals power, reputation is everything – and for women, one misstep can mean ruin.

Marquise de Merteuil, master in the art of survival, wields her influence with intelligence and control. Alongside the magnetic Vicomte de Valmont, they turn seduction into strategy and weaponise desire. But when their alliance collapses into rivalry, the battle between them threatens to destroy everyone in their path.

Lesley Manville (Oedipus, Phantom Thread) and Aidan Turner (Rivals) lead the company in a striking new staging of Christopher Hampton’s (The Father) celebrated adaptation of Choderlos de Laclos’ classic novel – a thrilling game of love, lies and social warfare, directed by Marianne Elliott (Angels in America).

“One of the most unique and enduring bands in alternative rock” —All Music “Margo Timmins’s voice is as melancholy and enchanting as ever” —The New York Times “There’s something that is nearly miraculous about the way Margo Timmins’ beautiful voice fits with those pained lyrics written by her brother Michael Timmins…the result is some truly transformative music.” —The Mercury News Cowboy Junkies will be performing a career-spanning show from The Trinity Session to their recent album, Such Ferocious Beauty!

In 1988, Cowboy Junkies proved that there was an audience waiting for something quiet, beautiful and reflective. The Trinity Session was like a whisper that cut through the noise — and it was compelling. It stood out in the midst of the flash and bombast that came to define the late ’80s. The now classic recording combined folk, blues and rock in a way that had never been heard before and went on to sell more than a million copies.

Formed in Toronto in 1985 with siblings Michael Timmins on guitar, Margo Timmins on vocals, Peter Timmins on drums, and Michael’s lifelong friend Alan Anton on bass, the band has sparkled over the course of 29 albums. “I’ve known Alan longer than I’ve known Pete,” says Michael. “We were friends before Pete was born.

Unlike most long-lasting groups, Cowboy Junkies have never had a break up or taken a sanity-saving hiatus. There’s an appreciation of each other that keeps them constantly working. “It’s that intimacy and understanding of what each one of us brings to the table,” says Michael. folkrockpop

events.title: Sean Mason Trio
about: $49 General Admission (plus processing fees)

“Mason’s music is exceptionally groovy.” —NPR Sean Mason stands as one of the most compelling and visionary artists to emerge from the jazz tradition in the 21st century—a jazz pianist and composer whose impact extends far beyond the bandstand. A Grammy Award nominee, Bessie Award winner, and Bistro Award recipient, Mason has distinguished himself not merely as a leading voice within the music, but as a cultural architect reshaping the genre’s relationship with style, movement, and artistic identity.

His artistry is defined by a rare duality: a deep knowledge of the jazz tradition and a philosophical commitment to the music as a human practice. Mason is drawn to the way jazz holds opposites in suspension—discipline and freedom, individuality and communion, thought and instinct—without forcing them into resolution. As Mason notes, “The beauty of the music is that it can hold contradiction without breaking. It can be refined and raw, structured and open, intimate and vast.” For Mason, jazz is not an act of presentation, but a condition of discovery, one in which meaning is formed in real time, and where musicians and listeners arrive together at something more truthful than either could have produced alone.

From his roots in Charlotte, North Carolina to the world stage, Mason’s trajectory reflects a steady and self-defined evolution. Shaped by formative experiences at Juilliard and within the lineage of the Marsalis tradition, he has developed a voice that is distinctly his own. Today, his impact is measured not only by his technical command, but by the way his influence shapes a new generation, one that reflects his sensibility in how they hear, move, and inhabit the music.

Mason’s recorded work traces a clear and deliberate artistic evolution. His debut, The Southern Suite, introduced a voice marked by depth and clarity, praised for its “spirit of celebration” and recognized as “a powerful introduction to Mason’s artistry and vision.” From the outset, critics noted both his maturity and individuality, describing the work as “forward-looking music” and “a bold statement of purpose from a generational talent.” That trajectory has only deepened. In moving tributes to legendary artists Piaf and Marlene Dietrich, singer-actress-director Rasooly and pianist Daniel Rein evoke the richly decadent world of 1920s-30s Berlin and Paris through their distinctive, theatrical approach to a varied repertoire of Berlin cabaret songs (think Kurt Weill!) and poetic French chansons. The program intertwines music and visual storytelling as Rasooly channels these legendary women of song through mime, elaborate costumes, and specially created life-size puppets, transporting us to a bygone era while illuminating timeless themes. Her storytelling combines a unique perspective of song, humor and puppetry that audiences will not soon forget.

events.title: The Longest Johns
about: Chart-topping folk group The Longest Johns are known the world over for their rollicking harmonies and raucous energy, blowing new wind into the sails of traditional sea shanties and work songs.

Formed in 2012 around a kitchen table in their native Bristol, the band bonded over a shared love of maritime folk music, wry humour, digital culture and their own songwriting. Ancient meets modern down by the docks.

Years of relentless touring, a strong online presence and a string of acclaimed releases helped them build a devoted global fanbase. Their breakout moment came in 2021 when their rendition of “Wellerman” went viral on TikTok, sparking the global “ShantyTok” phenomenon and igniting a worldwide resurgence in sea shanty music.

Over more than a decade, The Longest Johns have balanced preservation with reinvention. Their ambitious Pieces of Eight project saw the band release an EP every month for eight consecutive months, culminating in their tenth album. In 2024 they released the fan-funded album Voyage, accompanied by a book of original stories, artwork and lyrics. Voyage has since surpassed 7 million streams on Spotify. Across their catalogue the band now reach over 628,000 monthly listeners, generating more than 3.7 million streams every month.

Their new album Ends of the Earth sees the band pushing their signature vocal sound into new territories as they explore everything from the crimes of the eighteenth century to the monsters lurking in the vast wilderness of America. Expect beautiful harmonies, driving folk-rock and the sound of a band pushing themselves to their sonic limits.

The band continue to take folk music back to its roots by many routes. Proud digital natives and avid gamers, they performed at the opening of the 2025 Pokémon Europe International Championships where they debuted the track “Face the World” written especially for the event. They have also collaborated with the gaming community through appearances in the annual Jingle Jam hosted by The Yogscast and through their own streaming channel LongestJohnsGaming.

With over half a million YouTube subscribers and a global touring audience, The Longest Johns have travelled extensively across the UK, Europe, North America, Australia and New Zealand. In 2026 they will tour extensively across the UK, the United States, Europe and Canada, continuing to bring their powerful harmonies and modern take…

events.title: Peter Wolf and the Midnight Travelers
about: An evening with Peter Wolf and the incomparable Midnight Travelers…
Peter will be performing songs from his entire career…from the J. Geils Band to his critically acclaimed solo recordings, and so much more!

Peter Wolf has been known for decades as the dynamic lead singer and song writer of the J. Geils Band, with whom he showcased his talents on such hits as “Centerfold,” “Freeze Frame,” “Love Stinks” and “Musta Got Lost.”
Wolf’s musical roots precede rock ‘n’ roll and are inspired by his friendships and performances with such distinguished artists as Muddy Waters, John Lee Hooker and Van Morrison.

His solo career has produced critically acclaimed recordings that include duets with legendary performers such as Mick Jagger, Keith Richards, Aretha Franklin, Merle Haggard, Steve Earle and Neko Case.
Together with his distinguished band, “The Midnight Travelers”, Wolf is known for his ability to create an intimate and personal connection with his audience.

events.title: Béla Fleck: My Bluegrass Heart
about: Over the last four decades, Béla Fleck has made a point of boldly going where no banjo player has gone before, a musical journey that has earned him 19 Grammys in nine different fields, including Country, Pop, Jazz, Instrumental, Classical and World Music. But his roots are in bluegrass, and that’s where he returns with his celebrated bluegrass project, My Bluegrass Heart. The Grammy award-winning album, My Bluegrass Heart is the third chapter of a trilogy which began with the 1988 album, Drive, and continued in 1991 with The Bluegrass Sessions. Fleck’s band spotlights a multi-generational gamut of the best of bluegrass players, all sporting a myriad of Grammy Awards and nominations, as well as gigantic piles of IBMA awards for their instruments: fiddler Michael Cleveland, mandolinist Dominick Leslie, Jeff Partin on dobro, bassist/multi-instrumentalist Mark Schatz, and Jake Stargel on guitar.

Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.
1 hr 56 mins · R

events.title: Thunderbeard
about: Turn up the volume and step into the smoky, riff-driven world of Texas blues rock as ThunderBeard brings the gritty swagger of ZZ Top to the stage. With authentic showmanship, signature beards and plenty of guitar, ThunderBeard recreates the raw energy of “That Little Ol’ Band from Texas,” delivering a live experience that captures the attitude, sound and cool that defined a generation.

events.title: Americans We: The Eagles Community Band at 90
about: The Eagles Band comes to the Colonial to present Americans We, a celebratory concert of two anniversaries. The first half of the program is the finale to the Semiquincentennial year they have all been observing. It includes music rooted in our country’s history, with works by John Williams, Lin-Manuel Miranda, a salute to American jazz, and "Tribute to America" by director David Diggs.

events.title: Wandering Dance Festival

events.title: Warren Miller's Days Off

events.title: The Little Mermen & The Princess Pals: Disney Sing Along The Ultimate Disney Tribute Band
about: Recognized around the world as the #1 Disney tribute band—praised by Disney, ABC News, and more—The Little Mermen bring Disney’s most beloved songs to life with a rock-infused twist. Known for their high-energy performances, dazzling costumes, and Broadway-caliber vocals, the band delivers a nostalgic, joy-filled journey through a century of Disney magic, from Mary Poppins and The Lion King to modern favorites like Frozen and Moana

events.title: Special Guest Gallery Chat: Exploring BeHere / 1942 with Margaret Yee
about: Special Guest Gallery Chat: Exploring BeHere / 1942 with Margaret Yee Join us in our latest special exhibition, BeHere / 1942: A New Lens on the Japanese American Incarceration, for a special walkthrough with museum educator and Gallery Chats facilitator Margaret Yee.

Margaret will explore media representation and the impact of the language used to describe this historical moment as she guides visitors through this powerful artist’s rendition, centering the augmented reality (AR) components of the show. In this exhibition, creator and Japanese artist Masaki Fujihata enlarges and activates images by Dorothea Lange and Russell Lee, who documented the forced incarceration, encouraging visitors to look more closely at the emotions of each subject and the power dynamics at play between the photographer behind the camera and the people in front of it.
Concluding the talk, Margaret will share a poetry exercise highlighting the poem “Evacuation” by Mitsuye Yamada. Please join us for this deeper look into the history behind this amazing exhibition.
Get Museum Admission Tickets · Member Tickets

Margaret Yee has been volunteering at OMCA since 2017, first as a docent in the Gallery of California History and now as a School Programs and Gallery Chats Facilitator. A former high school teacher and museum educator, Margaret enjoys doing Gallery Chats because she loves the OMCA community and always learns something new from every conversation she has with a visitor.

events.title: Closing of Fairyland @ 75: A Legacy of Magic
about: Closing of Fairyland @ 75: A Legacy of Magic With just a few weeks left to experience it, OMCA welcomes you to explore Fairyland’s rich history and impact on Oakland’s cultural landscape with Fairyland @ 75: A Legacy of Magic.

Explore a timeline of Fairyland’s journey, a “then-and-now” look at beloved park attractions, and a glimpse into the park’s bright future. Visitors will discover miniatures created by local artists, photos of Magic Keys through the decades, and one of Fairyland’s original Jolly Trolly cars for kids and families to climb aboard. Don’t miss this celebration of Fairyland’s lasting legacy and role in shaping Oakland’s cultural landscape before the feature closes.

For over six decades, pioneering artist Ha Chong-Hyun (b. 1935) has explored what painting becomes when freed from all existing conventions. Ha’s work prizes the interaction of his materials: using pressure, gravity, and tools ranging from torches to everyday utensils, he transforms the surfaces of canvases up to eight feet tall into a treasure trove of texture and physicality. His first museum exhibition in North America, Ha Chong-Hyun: Retrospective offers an unprecedented look at the creative evolution of one of Korea’s most influential contemporary artists.

From his birth as a precious egg to his decision to serve as the vehicle of the Hindu god Vishnu, the divine adventures of Garuda come to life in this evocative exhibition. Part-bird, part-man, and the epitome of loyalty and courage, Garuda holds profound significance not only as a fierce warrior, but as the archetype of a deeply devoted son.

Featuring wooden sculptures and traditional paintings from the late 19th and early 20th centuries, the exhibition traces Garuda’s legendary exploits, capturing both the artistic mastery of Balinese creators and the enduring spiritual resonance of a protector deity who remains central to Indonesian culture today.

Beyond the ancient temples of Angkor lies a deeply compelling contemporary art scene. This exhibition spotlights works by Sopheap Pich and Leang Seckon, two of Cambodia’s most internationally prominent artists. Born in the 1970s, both lived through the Khmer Rouge genocide and emerged in the early 2000s as key figures in the country’s artistic revival.

Spotlight Sundays: Japanese American Legacies of Resistance Program | 1–2:30 pm Call to Action | 2:30–3:30 pm
All-Inclusive Ticket

This Sunday, we are stepping into the historical legacy that inspired OMCA’s latest special exhibition, BeHere / 1942: A New Lens on the Japanese American Incarceration. With opening remarks by OMCA Executive Director Lori Fogarty, we will engage with this present moment in American history with the clarity and learnings of the past.

Guest speakers Satsuki Ina and Miya Sommers, who both have personal or familial ties to wartime incarceration, will be joined in conversation by host Joemy Ito-Gates to explore how the shadows of this history led them to paths of anti-imperialist organizing, solidarity anchored in love, and healing work in times of enduring racial injustice. TaikoPeace will close the day with an interactive performance of “Ei Ja Nai Ka,” honoring Japanese American immigrant ancestors of this era and the echoes of their resistance through taiko, dance, and song. Come ready to learn, engage, and connect with one another!

Visitors are invited to continue the conversation during a post-program Call to Action gathering. Japanese American Families for Justice, Nikkei Resisters, and Tsuru for Solidarity will facilitate interactive protest art activities and share resources on how to get involved with current campaigns.
This program is a part of our exhibition programming for BeHere / 1942: A New Lens on the Japanese American Incarceration, on view through December 27, 2026.

Harun Farocki’s influential 2003 essay film and Mahmoud Alhaj’s recent videos examine how perception is controlled as a result, or a tool, of war and conflict.

events.title: Curator’s Tour / Anthony Graham on Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing
about: Senior Curator Anthony Graham offers a tour of Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing which he co-curated with Chief Curator Margot Norton. Author of the lead exhibition catalogue essay, Graham will explore the evolution of Hassinger's practice through her material experiments in sculpture, her long-standing engagement with movement and performance, and her work with the moving image.

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing
about: Included with admission.

Graduate students from the Departments of African American and African Diaspora Studies and History of Art offer exhibition tours on selected Wednesdays at 12:15 PM, Sundays at 2 PM, and Free First Thursdays at 1:15 PM.

events.title: Wrenching News Workshops
about: Included with admission.

Join artist Julia Goodman in creating Wrenching News, a collaborative artwork featured in Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing, through the process of twisting and knotting newspapers according to Hassinger’s specifications.

events.title: The Secret
about: Digital Restoration

Loosely based on a real-life double-murder case, Ann Hui’s grisly debut feature traces the labyrinthine investigation by one of the victim’s friends, played by Sylvia Chang. At once procedural and spectral, The Secret “thrives on pure cinematic wizardry” (Faith Everard, Senses of Cinema).

events.title: Mean Streets
about: 4K Digital Restoration

Set during the Feast of San Gennaro in the Italian neighborhood where Martin Scorsese grew up, and populated with characters and situations based on the neighborhood’s inhabitants, Mean Streets is a brilliant distillation of the themes that would define the director’s career.

events.title: Harakiri
about: Tatsuya Nakadai is a penniless samurai who asks a wealthy clan's permission to commit ritual suicide—though that’s not the only killing on his mind. “Probably the best samurai film ever made” (Washington Post).

events.title: Kwaidan
about: 4K Digital Restoration, Director’s Cut

This is Masaki Kobayashi’s atmospheric and visually captivating adaptation of four haunting stories by Lafcadio Hearn. “Each of the exquisitely crafted tales . . . is, in its own right, one of the great ghost stories brought to the screen. Together, they form an exemplar of the anthology horror film” (Village Voice).

events.title: The Sword
about: “With its blend of melodrama, weapons-based action, and wire-fu choreography . . . [The Sword] gets as swept up by the characters’ quieter moments of their muted agony as it does by their physical violence” (Jake Cole, Slant Magazine).

events.title: Mapping Utopias
about: Space is limited; RSVP required.

Educator, anthropologist, and community organizer Isa Prieto leads participants through a discussion and collective mapmaking activity exploring the idea of utopianism and the fragments of utopia that already live in our neighborhoods.

events.title: The Human Condition I: No Greater Love
about: Masaki Kobayashi’s three-part antiwar masterpiece follows the awakening—and disillusionment—of a Japanese soldier (the great Tatsuya Nakadai) during World War II. “Amazingly powerful in its emotional sweep and the depth of its historical insight. . . . Kobayashi’s monumental film can clarify and enrich your understanding of what it is to be alive” (New York Times).

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Some Particular Heaven: Ideas of Utopia in the BAMPFA Collection
about: Included with admission.

events.title: Contempt
about: 4K Digital Restoration
Jean-Luc Godard’s Homeric homage to Fritz Lang, “one of the defining moments of modernist filmmaking” (Film Comment). With Brigitte Bardot, Michel Piccoli, and Jack Palance.

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing
about: Included with admission.

Graduate students from the Departments of African American and African Diaspora Studies and History of Art offer exhibition tours on selected Wednesdays at 12:15 PM, Sundays at 2 PM, and Free First Thursdays at 1:15 PM.

events.title: Samurai Rebellion
about: Japanese cinema icons Toshiro Mifune and Tatsuya Nakadai team up to slice their way through duty-bound Japan in this tale of a dutiful samurai whose attempts to be a “good servant” are about to end . . . in blood.

events.title: Band of Outsiders
about: Digital Restoration

Anna Karina, Sami Frey, and Claude Brasseur are unlikely burglars in Jean-Luc Godard’s “reverie of a gangster movie” (Pauline Kael). “Band of Outsiders shows Godard at his most amusing, and that is no small thing” (Keneth Turan, Los Angeles Times).

events.title: Waikiki Brothers
about: A mediocre nightclub cover band strums its way across the forgotten hinterlands of South Korea in Yim Soon-rye’s now-cult classic—simultaneously deadpan and admiring, sorrowful and life-affirming—with lead roles for future superstars Hwang Jung-min and Ryoo Seung-bum.

events.title: The Inheritance
about: BAMPFA Collection

A dying businessman sets off a family scandal by announcing that his fortune will go to his illegitimate children in Masaki Kobayashi’s melodrama, a wry condemnation of Japanese postwar materialism, perfectly chilled by Toru Takemitsu’s jazzy score.

events.title: Artists’ Conversation: Emory Douglas and William Rhodes
about: Tickets required. Gallery admission included with ticket purchase.

In a conversation moderated by Sita Kuratomi Bhaumik, Emory Douglas and William Rhodes discuss their collaborative piece Revolution in Our Lifetime, featured in Some Particular Heaven, and unpack how art can foster solidarity, reimagine collective power, and help realize new political possibilities.

events.title: Taxi Driver
about: 4K Digital Restoration

After he takes a job as a taxi driver to cope with chronic insomnia, ex-Marine Travis Bickle (Robert “You talkin’ to me” De Niro) begins to see the dark city as one vast cesspool of crime and concupiscence.

events.title: Little Forest
about: A young professional abandons a Seoul life of coffee shops and office drudgery to return to a rural mountain farm and learn to “make her own time” in this “small film with a very big heart” (Taipei Times). Based on a Japanese manga.

events.title: The Human Condition II: The Road to Eternity
about: In Part II of Masaki Kobayashi’s nine-hour epic about Japan’s occupation of China during World War II, soldier Tatsuya Nakadai tries to institute more humane procedures in his military unit, but he only succeeds in attracting the ire of his fellow officers.

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing
about: Included with admission.

Graduate students from the Departments of African American and African Diaspora Studies and History of Art offer exhibition tours on selected Wednesdays at 12:15 PM, Sundays at 2 PM, and Free First Thursdays at 1:15 PM.

events.title: Communal Land Care with TERREMOTO and Test Plot
about: Landscape architecture design studio TERREMOTO and nonprofit Test Plot discuss their approach to radical communal land care that cultivates beauty and biodiversity, and explore the belief that ecological and climate crises require a repairing of kinship with our lands and a return to the commons and to care.

events.title: Just Like Weather
about: 4K Digital Restoration

Just Like Weather centers on a young couple on the rocks. Through interviews, reenacted scenes from their everyday lives, fictional episodes, and behind-the-scenes documentary, anxieties of Hong Kong’s future after 1997 bubble to the surface. “Fong has an unerring feel for the ways that people speak, think, laugh, console and wound each other” (Tony Rayns).

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Some Particular Heaven: Ideas of Utopia in the BAMPFA Collection
about: Included with admission.

events.title: Black Hole Collective Film Lab
about: This screening brings together films made by Black Hole Collective Film Lab members past and present, footage from group workshops taught by members and visiting artists, and documentation of the lab’s evolution through multiple moves over more than a decade.

events.title: La Chinoise
about: Digital Restoration
Jean-Luc Godard’s 1967 Pop-agitprop portrait of revolutionary youth “feels like a trial run for the May 1968 revolution. See it by any means necessary” (Time Out New York).

events.title: Harakiri
about: Tatsuya Nakadai is a penniless samurai who asks a wealthy clan's permission to commit ritual suicide—though that’s not the only killing on his mind. “Probably the best samurai film ever made” (Washington Post).

events.title: CineSpin: He Who Gets Slapped
about: Free admission. Tickets available at the admissions desk beginning at 6:30 PM.

Join us for CineSpin, the BAMPFA Student Committee’s annual event featuring terrific UC Berkeley student musicians providing original live accompaniment to great movies. This year the Berkeley Nu Jazz Collective will accompany Victor Sjöström’s He Who Gets Slapped, starring Lon Chaney.

events.title: Panel on Hassinger’s Moving Image Work: Leigh Raiford and Zana Sanders in Conversation with Robyn Farrell and Kristin Juarez
about: Tickets required. Gallery admission included with ticket purchase.

BAMPFA will present several of Maren Hassinger’s video works, from documentation of her early performance works to her later, more cinematic works. Following the screening, a panel will discuss Hassinger’s unique approach to the moving image across her career.

events.title: Samurai Rebellion
about: Japanese cinema icons Toshiro Mifune and Tatsuya Nakadai team up to slice their way through duty-bound Japan in this tale of a dutiful samurai whose attempts to be a “good servant” are about to end . . . in blood.

events.title: Raging Bull
about: 4K Digital Restoration

The biography of boxer Jake LaMotta becomes a visceral meditation on existential suffering. “A fusion of Hollywood genre with personal vision . . . closer to poetry than pulp. Its sculptural weight can only be appreciated on the big screen” (Amy Taubin, Village Voice).

events.title: The Human Condition III: A Soldier’s Prayer
about: By Part III of Masaki Kobayashi’s epic, the Japanese army is being routed by superior Russian troops. Protagonist Tatsuya Nakadai is captured by the Soviets and imprisoned, learning the bitter truth about the Red Army as liberators.

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing
about: Included with admission.

Graduate students from the Departments of African American and African Diaspora Studies and History of Art offer exhibition tours on selected Wednesdays at 12:15 PM, Sundays at 2 PM, and Free First Thursdays at 1:15 PM.

events.title: Rouge
about: Digital Restoration

Fleur (Anita Mui) is a ghost adrift in modern Hong Kong searching for her lost lover, “Twelfth Master” (Leslie Cheung). Slipping back and forth in time, “to watch Rouge today is to be reminded that cinema is a time machine: a repository of the dead, a record of losses, but also its own form of afterlife” (Dennis Lim, Criterion Collection).

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing
about: Included with admission.

Graduate students from the Departments of African American and African Diaspora Studies and History of Art offer exhibition tours on selected Wednesdays at 12:15 PM, Sundays at 2 PM, and Free First Thursdays at 1:15 PM.

events.title: The Last Waltz
about: 4K Digital Restoration

Martin Scorsese’s loving portrait of The Band’s farewell concert in San Francisco is “arguably the most beautiful of rock movies, while the musical highlights . . . still astound” (Time Out). With guest appearances by Eric Clapton, Bob Dylan, Joni Mitchell, and more.

events.title: Center Stage
about: 4K Digital Restoration

Maggie Cheung stars in Stanley Kwan’s modernist biopic on the life and tragic early death of Chinese film star Ruan Lingyu. “A masterpiece . . . the greatest Hong Kong film I’ve seen” (Jonathan Rosenbaum).

events.title: Bellissima
about: 4K Digital Restoration
Luchino Visconti is in an unusually comic mode for this satire on urban life and movieland ambition. The incomparable Anna Magnani plays a mother trying to launch her young daughter in show business.

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing
about: Included with admission.

Graduate students from the Departments of African American and African Diaspora Studies and History of Art offer exhibition tours on selected Wednesdays at 12:15 PM, Sundays at 2 PM, and Free First Thursdays at 1:15 PM.

events.title: White Nights
about: 4K Digital Restoration
Marcello Mastroianni stars in a romantic, sublimely artificial adaptation of a Fyodor Dostoyevsky story about people drifting along crossing, doubling paths.

events.title: GoodFellas
about: 4K Digital Restoration

Martin Scorsese’s adaptation of Nicholas Pileggi’s chronicle of real-life Mafia associate Henry Hill, hurtles through some twenty-five years of “family” life, as the riveting Ray Liotta inhabits Hill’s chilling and darkly humorous first-person account.
